name: Snowflake Marketplace
description: Snowflake Marketplace distributes provider-specific data products and Snowflake Native Apps through free, trial, paid, public, and private listings. Access and installation occur inside a customer's Snowflake organization and can carry provider terms, regional constraints, privileges, compute use, and charges.
agentUseSummary: Snowflake Marketplace cannot yet be connected through Relay. The marketplace is a catalog of independently governed data products and applications rather than one uniform data API. Relay has no approved listing, provider, account, region, legal terms, price, database objects, role, query, compute budget, or application-permission contract.

blocked.label: Connect Snowflake Marketplace
blocked.description: A customer account, authorized role, accepted Marketplace and listing terms, selected region and listing, warehouse, and constrained service identity are required.

blocked.label: Discover or install listings
blocked.description: Searching, requesting, trialing, purchasing, installing, upgrading, configuring, or removing data products and Native Apps is blocked.

blocked.label: Query marketplace data products
blocked.description: Listing databases, schemas, tables, views, functions, procedures, application data, telemetry, and provider-shared data remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Execute SQL or administer Snowflake
blocked.description: Arbitrary SQL, DDL, DML, grants, roles, users, warehouses, databases, applications, listings, shares, billing, and bulk extraction are blocked.

blocked.label: Use private or credential-based access
blocked.description: Browser automation, password or session capture, private keys, broad tokens, unapproved provider interfaces, and privilege probing are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Snowflake Marketplace action is enabled without one exact listing, provider, terms, price, region, object, query, role, warehouse, and cost-control contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No Snowflake Marketplace tools are mounted before listing-specific legal, data, role, compute, and cost boundaries are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: Snowflake Marketplace is a distribution and procurement channel for provider-specific shared datasets and Native Apps, not one uniform account-data service. Listings may be free, private, limited trial, paid, region-limited, or provider-approved, and they can carry additional legal terms and usage-based costs. Authorized organization users must accept Marketplace terms and hold privileges to acquire listings. Once installed, access occurs through account-specific database objects or Native Apps under customer roles and compute, while Snowflake's SQL API can execute most DDL and DML and administer deployments. A generic connector would conflate purchasing and terms acceptance with arbitrary SQL, provider data rights, app permissions, and customer compute spend.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, data, procurement, finance, legal, privacy, security, platform, audit, and customer owners must select one listing and freeze the provider, version, access type, price, trial, terms, region, data rights, retention, database objects, columns, allowed queries, Native App permissions, roles, warehouse, resource monitor, budgets, output handling, and incident duties. An authorized Snowflake administrator must then accept required terms, acquire the listing, and create a dedicated least-privilege service role and bounded warehouse. Only after that may Relay implement pinned typed read-only wrappers with allowlisted parameterized queries, result and cost limits, redaction, audit, and post-disable denial.

evidence.supports: Listings distribute provider data or Native Apps through free, trial, paid, public, and private access models with provider-specific availability.
Marketplace providers and consumers must accept additional Snowflake terms and comply with data-sharing and acceptable-use policies.
Consumers need organization-authorized terms acceptance and listing privileges; listings can cross regions and incur in-Snowflake payments.
The account-specific SQL API can query and update data and execute most DDL and DML, including deployment administration.
Snowflake API access is account-specific and supports key pairs, OAuth, programmatic tokens, or workload identities associated with customer users and roles.
